issues.legal_issue: Land reform provisions that restructure a landlord’s rights by allowing resumption of some land and transfer of other land to tenants modify property rights for purposes of constitutional protection.
material_facts: The challenged provisions allowed land to be determined as resumable or non-resumable.
The landlord could resume the resumable land for personal cultivation.
A tenant could acquire non-resumable land by paying compensation, and rights held by others in that land were extinguished.
issues.conclusion: The provisions modified the landlord’s substantive rights and fell within the protection of Article 31A(1) of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1) protects laws that modify rights in an estate. Following Atma Ram v. State of Punjab, modification of a landowner’s substantive rights can qualify even where the argument is that a right has been transferred rather than extinguished.

predicates.land_reform_challenge: A party challenged land reform provisions on constitutional grounds.
predicates.landlord_rights_restructured: The provisions allowed a landlord to resume some land and allowed tenants to acquire other land, thereby changing the landlord’s substantive rights.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns land reform provisions that restructure a landlord’s rights in this way, the provisions receive constitutional protection.

issues.legal_issue: The special market-value guarantee for land within an applicable ceiling limit does not apply when no ceiling limit is in force under law.
material_facts: The challenged land reform provisions included a chapter dealing with ceiling limits.
That chapter had not been brought into force by notification.
No other applicable ceiling limit was identified as being in force.
issues.conclusion: The second proviso to Article 31A(1) did not apply because no ceiling limit was applicable under law then in force.
issues.legal_principle: The second proviso to Article 31A(1) protects land within a ceiling limit applicable to the landholder under a law for the time being in force. A ceiling scheme that has not been brought into force does not supply an applicable ceiling limit.

predicates.constitutional_compensation_challenge: A party challenged the compensation payable under land reform provisions by relying on the constitutional guarantee for certain land acquisitions.
predicates.no_applicable_ceiling_limit: No ceiling limit applicable to the landholder was in force under law.

issues.definition: When a constitutional compensation challenge concerns land and no applicable ceiling limit is in force, the special market-value guarantee does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: Land cultivated by a crop-sharer for the crop-sharer’s own account is not land under the owner’s personal cultivation.
material_facts: The owner claimed that land cultivated under a crop-sharing tenure was under the owner’s personal cultivation.
The cultivator grew the crop in the cultivator’s own right and shared the crop with the owner.
The cultivator did not cultivate on behalf of the owner.
issues.conclusion: The crop-sharing land was not under the owner’s personal cultivation for purposes of the second proviso to Article 31A(1).
issues.legal_principle: For the second proviso to Article 31A(1), personal cultivation means cultivation by or on behalf of the owner. A crop-sharer who cultivates in the crop-sharer’s own right does not cultivate on behalf of the owner.

predicates.constitutional_compensation_challenge: A party relied on the constitutional protection for land under an owner’s personal cultivation in a compensation challenge.
predicates.crop_share_tenure: The land was cultivated under an arrangement in which the cultivator shared the crop with the owner.
predicates.cultivator_cultivates_for_self: The cultivator worked the land in the cultivator’s own right rather than on behalf of the owner.

issues.definition: When land is cultivated by a crop-sharer for the crop-sharer’s own account, it is not treated as the owner’s personal cultivation.

issues.legal_issue: Courts ordinarily should not decide the validity of a statutory provision before it has been brought into force and can be enforced.
material_facts: The challenged chapter had not been brought into force by notification.
The chapter was therefore dormant and could not be enforced.
The High Court had considered and ruled on the chapter’s validity.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have considered the validity of the dormant chapter, and the Court did not decide whether that chapter was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Courts ordinarily should not decide the validity of an Act or provision before it is brought into force, because the question is academic while the provision remains dormant and unenforceable. The Court referred to State of Orissa v. Chander Sekhar.

predicates.validity_challenge_to_statutory_provisio: A party asked a court to decide whether a statutory provision was constitutionally valid.
predicates.provision_not_in_force: The provision had not been brought into force.
predicates.provision_cannot_be_enforced: The provision could not be applied or enforced while it remained dormant.

issues.definition: When a validity challenge concerns a provision that is not in force and cannot be enforced, the court declines to decide its validity.

issues.legal_issue: A party bound by an earlier judgment cannot use a later appeal to seek reconsideration of the same decision.
material_facts: The appellant had been a party to an earlier Supreme Court decision concerning the validity of the challenged chapter.
The appellant sought reconsideration of that decision in the present appeal.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment was binding on the appellant, who could not seek its review in this manner.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment of the Supreme Court binds a party to that judgment; the party cannot obtain its reconsideration by raising the same matter in a later appeal.

predicates.later_appeal_reopens_previously_decided_: A party used a later appeal to seek reconsideration of an issue already decided.
predicates.appellant_bound_by_prior_judgment: The party seeking reconsideration was bound by the earlier judgment on that issue.

issues.definition: When a party bound by an earlier judgment seeks to reopen the same issue in a later appeal, the court rejects that attempt.
